caption: The post-training process described in Appendix <ref> decreases hallucinations. One measure is that the problems in SimpleQA—which the model very rarely gets correct—are increasingly not attempted during the course of post-training. We believe the final result is better behavior, even though the simple-evals score for SimpleQA (the F1 score) actually gives our base model a higher score than our final model.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the SimpleQA performance over the course of post-training, showing the distribution of responses across different categories at four stages: Base, SFT, DPO Stage 1, and Final. The horizontal axis displays the post-training stages, listed in sequential order. The vertical axis represents percentage, ranging from 0 to 100, with tick labels at intervals of 20. Each stage is represented by a set of stacked bars, with three distinct categories: Correct (green), Not Attempted (blue), and Incorrect (light blue).  The "Base" stage shows a green bar with a value of 3.2%, a blue bar of 6.8%, and a light blue bar of 90.0%. The "SFT" stage displays a green bar of 57.5%, a blue bar of 3.7%, and a light blue bar of 38.7%.  The "DPO Stage 1" stage contains a green bar with a value of 79.8%, a blue bar of 2.9%, and a light blue bar of 17.4%. Finally, the "Final" stage comprises a green bar of 81.1%, a blue bar of 3.0%, and a light blue bar of 15.8%. Annotated percentages are displayed directly above each bar. No bars are visually emphasized beyond the color distinctions representing the response categories.
